merger_description:
OceanaGold Corporation (via its wholly-owned Australian subsidiary OceanaGold (Australia) Pty Ltd) (together, **OceanaGold**) is proposing to acquire 100% of the issued shares of Ausgold Limited (**Ausgold**), through a scheme of arrangement (the **Acquisition**).

OceanaGold is a global intermediate gold and copper mining company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX:OGC) and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE:OGC). OceanaGold’s principal mining operations are located in the United States of America (Haile Gold Mine), New Zealand (Macraes Operation and Waihi Operation) and the Philippines (Didipio Mine). OceanaGold does not hold, operate or have an interest in any gold mining or exploration tenements in Australia. However, OceanaGold supplies gold that has been produced overseas to customers in Australia.

Ausgold is an ASX-listed (ASX:AUC) development-stage gold mining company. Its principal asset is the Katanning Gold Project, located in Western Australia. As a development-stage project, Ausgold does not currently produce or sell gold.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. there is no current horizontal overlap between OceanaGold
and Ausgold in the supply and production of gold in Australia
b. the parties’ actual and expected combined share in the
production and supply of gold in Australia and globally is low
and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition is expected to be small
c. the presence of alternative producers and suppliers of gold
in Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
